reason: Fixes tests/integration/test_ambient.py::test_ingest_does_not_wait_on_a_slow_honcho, which proved the opposite of its name (issue #74). Its fake was `slow_feed(peer_id, text)` while nora/ingest/stages/memory_feed.py has called `feed(peer_id=, text=, conversation_id=, metadata=)` since 2026-08-07 - so the fake raised TypeError immediately inside the spawned task, and the only assertion, elapsed wall time under 0.2s, was satisfied by a call that never slept. The 1.0s sleep the test is named for never happened. It surfaced as an intermittent failure because the background task's error log lands in this test's capture only under the full serial suite, so the same deterministic defect looked like a flake. Fixed by giving the fake production's signature and adding a positive control that the fake was actually ENTERED - after one loop tick, since the feed is spawned and has not started when on_event returns, which is the property the elapsed time is about. Reverting the signature reddens it. Test-only; no production code touched.
